long_biography.plain_text:
A severe back injury during his school years left Michael Bassem Rimlawi with chronic pain and pushed him towards spinal medicine. He completed an osteopathic medical degree, an orthopaedic residency and fellowship training that combined orthopaedic and neurosurgical approaches at the University of California, San Diego.

Rimlawi established a Dallas outpatient practice around smaller-incision procedures. He became an early adopter of lateral interbody fusion and camera-assisted lumbar fusion, while advising device manufacturers and presenting new methods to fellow surgeons. The practice combined complex cervical, lumbar and scoliosis operations with less invasive approaches designed to reduce tissue disruption and recovery time.

uncertainties.detail: The Texas Medical Board revoked Rimlawi's licence in 2021 after imprisonment following a felony conviction. Several current-looking directories and exact-name promotional sites nevertheless describe him as practising. Those later claims are not used to establish active licensure, and both biographies use historical career wording.

The spine institute is the only clearly evidenced principal business associated with Rimlawi, but reviewed sources do not establish his present ownership percentage or control after 2021. Healthcare is therefore retained as the disclosed origin-sector fallback for primary industry.

Rimlawi described an obstetrician father and nurse mother who influenced his medical ambitions. No source reviewed identifies a transferred practice, inherited business stake or family financing, so the broad Self-made value is used without an independent-start subtype and without inferring family succession.

Dated age statements from December 2016, February 2018 and May 2020 converge uniquely on 1971, which is proposed as a reasoned inference. No reliable source located establishes the birth day, month or place, so those fields remain unproposed.

The source record identifies Rimlawi as American. A self-promotional profile describes Italian and Lebanese paternal background, but ancestry does not establish citizenship; no secondary nationality is proposed.

The 2015 RD Yacht Management filing strongly supports the historical owner identity, but Denison records a 2020 sale of Negoseator while the source relationship remains marked current. This dossier flags the conflict without changing owner-vessel data or using the yacht in either biography.

Inventor is assigned because multiple patents and independent career coverage make invention a defining practiced role. Medical devices is not assigned because the available record does not show that device ownership or operations created material wealth or constituted a substantial controlled business.

Several exact-name domains published similar biographies and current-practice material in 2025. None was independently linked from a verified first-party account, and some current clinical wording conflicts with the official licence record, so no personal website is proposed.
